solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tiniest square by shopping centre is in Paris

parts.note: S is a standard abbreviation for square, as in sq or S on plans
a mall is a shopping centre
est is French for 'is'

explanation.surface: A tiny Parisian square sits beside a shopping centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' tells you to give the French word for 'is', which is EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are superlatives meaning of the very least size.

clue.text: Snub Flimsy

definitions.meaning: to snub someone is to insult them by ignoring them, a verb sense
flimsy means thin, frail or insubstantial, an adjective sense

explanation.surface: The setter, Flimsy, signs the clue by snubbing the solver.
explanation.walkthrough: Flimsy is also the setter's pseudonym, so the second definition doubles as a signature.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to cold-shoulder; as an adjective it means slender or weak.

clue.text: Bill may drive east out of place

indicators.note: letters that are out of place are not in their proper positions, so these get rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Bill might drive eastward when he is somewhere he does not belong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is the verb, to bill as in to promote. 'out of place' rearranges DRIVE EAST.
explanation.definitionFit: To bill a show is to promote or announce it publicly, a synonym.

clue.text: Promise to remove top shelf

indicators.note: taking off the top of a down word removes its first letter, here the initial P

parts.note: a pledge is a promise

explanation.surface: Someone vows to take the top shelf away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to remove top' takes the first letter P off PLEDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow flat projection from a wall or cliff is a shelf, a synonym.

clue.text: Grazed from fight with editor

parts.note: a scrap is a fight or scuffle

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor came out of a scuffle with a graze.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin that has been scraped has been grazed, a synonym for a minor surface wound.

clue.text: Homeless animals king keeps outside

indicators.note: the word for keeps sits outside the king, so it wraps around his letter

parts.note: stays means keeps or remains, as in 'keeps calm' and 'stays calm'
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A king keeps stray animals out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts STAYS around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Strays are pets or livestock that have wandered off and lack a home.

clue.text: Tense composer left on ferry regularly — one's touring?

indicators.note: in a down clue, the earlier pieces are placed on top of the letters from ferry

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
Maurice Ravel was a French composer

indicators.note: taking letters regularly picks every other one of ferry, here its second and fourth

explanation.surface: A tense composer goes left on a ferry, apparently while on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of FERRY, giving ER, which go under T, RAVEL and L. The definition reads 'one is touring'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tours from place to place is a voyager, so one who is touring fits; the question mark flags the loose phrasing.

clue.text: No.10 character in miscalculated social gathering almost isolated

indicators.note: the tenth character of the word miscalculated is picked out
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a party is a social gathering

explanation.surface: A Downing Street figure at a badly planned party was left almost alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No.10' suggests Downing Street; here it means the tenth letter of 'miscalculated', A. 'almost' drops the Y from PARTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Set apart means separated or isolated from others, a synonym.

clue.text: Put up with a road's quality

parts.note: to stand something is to put up with it
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates the quality of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a level of quality, as in a high standard of work.

clue.text: Attackers damage hired vans, wanting hospital

indicators.note: to damage something is to break it up, so the letters are rearranged
wanting means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Raiders smash up rented vans while short of a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' drops H from HIRED VANS, and 'damage' rearranges IREDVANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Invaders are those who attack and enter a territory, so a synonym.

clue.text: A bloke returned wearing father's hat

indicators.note: a garment being worn sits inside the wearer's outline, so father wraps around the other letters

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a bloke is a man

explanation.surface: A man came back with his dad's hat on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' looks like it belongs with the hat in the surface; it means the reversed bloke and A sit inside father.
explanation.definitionFit: A Panama is a brimmed straw hat, so an example of headwear.

clue.text: Activity, whichever way you look at it

definitions.note: the definition word itself, which this palindromic answer also defines

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: reading the word forwards or backwards gives the same letters, so it works either way

parts.note: the definition word itself, which this palindromic answer also defines

explanation.surface: An activity looks the same however you view it.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is an act or action, a synonym for an activity done.

clue.text: Nag husband or lovemaking is cut short

indicators.note: cutting a word short lops off its final letter

parts.note: sex is lovemaking

explanation.surface: A wife nags her husband because lovemaking keeps being curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' looks like a verb about complaining; it is the noun, an old horse. 'is cut short' drops the X from SEX.
explanation.definitionFit: A nag is an informal word for an old or worn-out horse.

clue.text: Harbour a grudge about Edward after penny's handed over

indicators.note: the grudge and Edward come after the penny

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for penny
to resent is to harbour a grudge
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Someone resents Edward once a penny has changed hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Something presented has been given or handed over formally, a synonym.

clue.text: Caught tucking into alcoholic drink, daughter grimaced

indicators.note: tucking into means getting inside, so the caught letter goes inside the drink

parts.note: wine is an alcoholic drink
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A daughter was caught drinking and pulled a face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' puts C inside WINE, and D follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To wince is to flinch or pull a pained face, so a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Model all clothes initially with a cute figure

indicators.note: to model is to shape or form, so these letters are moulded into a new order

parts.words: all clothes initially with a cute
parts.note: the word all, the first letter of clothes (initially), and the words a cute, pooled together as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A model whose clothes all show off a cute figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like the fashion model; it is the anagram signal for ALL, the C from 'clothes initially' and A CUTE. 'figure' is the verb, as in work out.
explanation.definitionFit: To figure something is to work it out by reckoning, so a synonym.

clue.text: Be hugged by the German for free

indicators.note: a thing hugged by another is held inside it

parts.note: der is a German word for 'the'
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: A command to let a German embrace you, and you are set free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be' looks like the verb of the instruction; it stands for LIVE, as in to be or exist.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone from captivity is to free them, a synonym (verb).

clue.text: Sailor under six barrels, trembling

indicators.note: in a down clue, the sailor goes under the other pieces

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
B is an abbreviation for barrels, as in measures of oil
a rating is a non-commissioned sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor beneath six barrels is shaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shaking rapidly back and forth is quivering, a synonym.

clue.text: Definitely wearing suit

parts.note: to be in something is to be wearing it, as in 'in a hat'
spades is a suit of cards

explanation.surface: Someone is certainly wearing a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing, which 'wearing' supports; it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning to a great degree or emphatically, so it fits definitely.

clue.text: Gets to what's required for vaccinations?

definitions.meaning: to get to someone is to irritate or annoy them
the sharp hollow instruments used for jabs, with the question mark flagging a descriptive definition

explanation.surface: Vaccinations get under people's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means annoys persistently; as a plural noun it names the sharp points injections are given through.

clue.text: Cut legs climbing

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word reads upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: pins is informal for legs

explanation.surface: Legs get cut while climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reads PINS upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A small quick cut with scissors is a nip of the blade, a synonym (noun or verb).

clue.text: Scours hotel for 100 plants

indicators.note: one thing put in for another replaces it

parts.note: to scour is to scrub
C is the Roman numeral for 100
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A cleaner scours a hotel to earn a hundred, among the plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' puts H in place of C in SCRUBS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushes are woody plants, so the answer names an example of plants.

clue.text: Son, for example, intended to leave a portion

indicators.note: a letter left behind is removed from the word

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A son, say, was meant to leave a share behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' removes A from MEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is a section or piece of a whole, a synonym.

clue.text: Poor person's urge to enter pub

indicators.note: going in means one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a bar is a pub
to egg someone on is to urge them

explanation.surface: A poor man feels the urge to go into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'urge' is the verb, as in to egg someone on.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lives by asking for alms is destitute, so a poor person.

clue.text: Provoking cop in drug bust

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A policeman is goaded during a drugs raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like a police raid, which fits the surface; it signals rearranging COP IN DRUG.
explanation.definitionFit: To prod someone is to provoke or goad them, so a synonym.

clue.text: Retreat from old American relative

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a relative

explanation.surface: Fleeing from an elderly American relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreat' looks like a verb about fleeing; it is the noun, a refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: A haven or quiet refuge is a retreat, as in an oasis of calm.

clue.text: Decrepit car's constant speed

parts.note: c is the constant for the speed of light in physics
rate means speed

explanation.surface: An old banger can only keep up a steady pace.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the physics symbol for the speed of light, a constant.
explanation.definitionFit: Crate is informal slang for an old, rickety vehicle.

clue.text: Country clubs beginning to hamper fashionable area

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Country clubs start to hold back a trendy district.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the most populous nation in East Asia, an example of a country.

clue.text: Insult mother with large pants

definitions.note: British slang adjective meaning rubbish or very poor

parts.note: dis is slang for insult
ma is mother
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Mocking your mother for her big underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like underwear; it is British slang for rubbish, very poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal for gloomy or wretchedly poor in quality.

clue.text: Wanting dire sign rewritten

indicators.note: something rewritten has its contents set down again in a new order

explanation.surface: A dreadful notice is lacking and needs redoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanting something is longing for it, a synonym.

clue.text: Some wounds I sterilise?

indicators.note: some of these words means only part of their letters, a run inside them

explanation.surface: A hospital worker describes cleaning wounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a senior British nurse is called a sister, and sterilising wounds is her job.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a senior nurse is called by this title, the person who might say she cleans wounds.

clue.text: More rum, visitor?

definitions.meaning: rum is British slang for odd, so more rum means odder
a newcomer or someone unfamiliar who comes to a place

explanation.surface: A guest asks for another rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink; it is old British slang for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: As a comparative it means odder; as a noun it is an outsider or newcomer.
